result.description: SaaS ecommerce platform for merchants: catalog, orders, customers, carts, checkout, storefront, plus B2B Edition.
result.auth_detail: OAuth-based API accounts. Store-level accounts give a static access_token created in the control panel. App-level accounts come from the Developer Portal and use an OAuth install flow per store. Account-level accounts are used for the GraphQL Account API. Tokens are sent in the X-Auth-Token header. Legacy Basic-auth accounts are no longer issued.
result.access_detail: A store owner can create a store-level API account in any store, including a free trial store, so a developer gets a token with no review. Partners can also create sandbox stores in the Partner Portal. Listing a public app on the marketplace needs BigCommerce app review. The trial length (15 days) and whether a credit card is required are unverified, and sources conflict. I found no plan restriction on the API.
result.api_notes: REST Management API (V2 and V3) covers catalog, orders, customers, carts, checkout, pricing, promotions, webhooks and scripts. REST Storefront and GraphQL Storefront APIs cover shopper-side data. There is also a GraphQL Admin API, a GraphQL Account API and a B2B Edition REST API. Breadth is from search results and the API accounts page table, not a full endpoint count.

evidence.quote: BigCommerce no longer issues legacy API Accounts to new stores.
Rewrite your HTTP request headers to use the `X-Auth-Token` header to pass the API account's `access_token` instead of the `Authorization` header.
Sandbox stores are intended for developing and testing apps.
